28 BEST Places to Visit in Europe in DECEMBER!

November 24, 2026

What are the best places to visit in Europe in December? Whether you’re looking for Christmas related trips, cold weather, or some sunshine, I have you covered in this guide to December travel in Europe.

With schools breaking up for the Christmas holidays in December, this is an excellent time of the year to travel and the best thing about going on holiday in Europe in December is the amount of options there are!

The choice runs from festive city breaks and world-class ski slopes to warm places to visit in December, so there is something for every kind of trip.

⛄ Best Places for Snow and Northern Lights in December in Europe

These picks promise the best odds of snow at Christmas, along with a good chance of spotting the Northern Lights.

1. Rovaniemi, Finland

Set on the Arctic Circle in Finnish Lapland, Rovaniemi is the official hometown of Santa Claus, and Santa Claus Village lets you meet him and post a card from his office. Of all the things to do in Rovaniemi, snowmobiling, reindeer sledge rides and dog sledging stand out, so pack warm layers for days that rarely climb above freezing. Suggested by: Pamela from The Directionally Challenged Traveler

2. Reykjavik, Iceland

Iceland’s snowy capital gets only around four hours of daylight in December, which means frequent northern lights displays. Day trips along the Golden Circle to Þingvellir National Park or to Lake Kleifarvatn on the Reykjanes Peninsula are easy, and no trip to Iceland in December is complete without the lights and ice rink of Yule Town at Ingólfstorg. Suggested by: Victoria of Iceland Trippers

3. Alta, Norway

Nicknamed “the town of the Northern Lights”, the Norwegian town of Alta has just 20,000 residents yet is the biggest place in Finnmark County, reached by cruise ship, a two-hour flight from Oslo or a 5.5-hour drive from Tromso. Polar night from late November to mid-January leaves only a blue afternoon twilight, perfect for aurora hunting, with snowshoeing, dogsledding, the Northern Lights Cathedral, Alta Museum and the Sorrisniva ice hotel to fill the days. Suggested by: Roshni from The Wanderlust Within

4. Dolomites, Italy

Northern Italy’s jagged Dolomites pair excellent skiing with a fairytale Christmas setting. Pick a base such as Ortisei, Cortina or Val d’Ega, allow at least four days, and drive or take the train from Milan a few hours away; a car helps, and there are more than 20 ski resorts to choose from. Suggested by: Adam and Kathryn of Adventures of A+K

🎄Best Christmas Markets in Europe in December

Next up are the cities with the strongest Christmas market scenes.

5. Nuremberg, Germany

Nuremberg’s famous Christkindlesmarkt spreads across the old town all December, centred on the Hauptmarkt beside the gothic Frauenkirche. Churches, timber-framed houses and the Imperial Castle on the hill, which stays open in winter, make a fine backdrop. Suggested by: Rich from RJOnTour

6. Prague, Czechia

Prague’s markets usually open in late November and close on December 24th. The Old Town Square market has a giant tree, concerts, mulled wine and hot mead but draws the biggest crowds, while the smaller market at Náměstí míru outside the church of St. Ludmila is calmer, and Veronika’s favourite is the Prague Castle Christmas market beside St. Vitus Cathedral. Suggested by: Veronika from Travel Geekery

7. Budapest, Hungary

Affordable Budapest offers history, good food and beer, plus Christmas markets from late November through December selling local gifts, chimney cake, Palacsinta and marzipan. The largest is in Vörösmarty Square, where Hungarian bands give free concerts every day. Suggested by: Adam & Hannah from Getting Stamped

8 . Berlin, Germany

A highlight is the WeihnachtsZauber at Gendarmenmarkt, with festive food, mulled wine and stalls of gifts and ornaments, while Lucia at Kulturbrauerei brings a Nordic theme to a former brewery courtyard. Stay for New Year’s Eve to see one of the world’s biggest celebrations near Brandenburg Gate. Suggested by: Ali from Berlin Travel Tips

9. Halstatt, Austria

Lakeside Hallstatt, with its colourful homes on the slopes of the Alps, is a great family pick when lights and garlands decorate the village. From December 8th it hosts a Christmas market with handmade gifts, a life-sized wooden Nativity made by the local carpentry school, glühwein and the town’s well-known cookies. Suggested by: Jess from Uprooted Traveler

10. Lucerne, Switzerland

Lucerne’s old town glows with lights and Christmas markets, and snow makes the scenery even prettier. Take a boat on Lake Lucerne, ride the cogwheel train up Mount Pilatus for sledging and snowshoeing, or head for nearby ski resorts and skating on the frozen lakes. Suggested by: Lavina D’Souza from Continent Hop

11. London, U.K

London brings winter festivals, decorations and markets such as the Southbank Centre Winter Market and Covent Garden. Hyde Park Winter Wonderland, the light trail at Christmas at Kew and festive concerts at the Royal Albert Hall are other December favourites. Suggested by: Daniel from North Carolina Travel Guides

🏛️ Best City Breaks in Europe in December

These cities have a market or two, but they are worth visiting for far more than Christmas shopping.

12. Rome, Italy

Thinner December crowds make it easier to book the Colosseum, the Borghese Gallery and the Vatican, and to linger at Piazza Navona, the Pantheon and the Trevi Fountain. The city is lit up for the holidays, and its best Christmas market in Piazza Navona runs from 8 December to 6 January. Suggested by: Lisa Garrett of Waves and Cobblestones

13 . Lisbon, Portugal

Lisbon stays mild in December despite cooler days and some rain. Try festive treats like the sweet-potato Broas Castelares and Bolo Rei, enjoy the lights, and browse the market in Rossio Square for gifts, hot chocolate and roasted nuts. Suggested by: Nausheen of Globe Gazers

14 . Porto, Portugal

With peak season over, Porto is quieter, and its mild weather suits strolling with a cup of hot Port wine. Make time for the Art Nouveau Majestic Café, a local favourite since 1921, whose long summer queues shrink in winter. Suggested By: Megan From Traveller’s Elixir

15. Dubrovnik, Croatia

Dubrovnik is chilly but usually sunny in December, better for sightseeing than swimming. Explore its Baroque and Renaissance churches, monasteries, palaces and Old City walls without crowds, and catch the Dubrovnik Christmas Fair, when huts selling Croatian treats line Stradun. Suggested by: Milijana of World Travel Connector

16. Athens, Greece

Mild weather and far fewer visitors mean you can climb to the Acropolis without the summer crush, and the A.P. Acropolis View Apartments offer an indoor pool with views of it. Syntagma Square is lit up, and Technopolis hosts performances, food stalls and a Christmas market. Suggested by: Mal of Raw Mal Roams

17. Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina

The Baščaršija area of the Bosnian capital fills with lights and markets, and temperatures of -5°C to 5°C (23°F to 41°F) may bring snow. Locals head to the Olympic mountain towns of Bjelašnica and Jahorina for skiing, and with fewer tourists around the city is easy to explore. Suggested by: Ellis from Backpack Adventures

🌞 Best Places to Visit for some Sun in Europe in December

For winter sun, aim for the Canary Islands and the Mediterranean, but expect mild rather than hot weather anywhere in Europe this month.

For more ideas see my guide to 14 BEST Winter Sun Destinations in EUROPE

18. Gran Canaria, Spain

Daytime highs of about 22c/71f and a similar sea temperature keep swimming on the cards, though evenings and the mountains call for a light layer. Choose between the capital Las Palmas, the resort of Maspalomas beside its dunes, or quieter Taurito with its cliff-lined beach and saltwater waterpark. Suggested By: Kylie from Between England and Everywhere

19. Barcelona, Spain

Barcelona combines a city break with time by the sea; it is too cool to sunbathe, but a beach walk between Christmas and New Year was a highlight for us. Smaller crowds and comfortable temperatures make it easy to explore on foot, and the city felt only lightly Christmassy.

20. Malta

Cheap December flights and one of Europe’s warmest winter climates make Malta easy to reach and enjoy. Relax on its beaches, take a private boat trip to hidden lagoons and coves, and get around by public transport or hire car. Suggested by: Lowri from Many Other Roads

21. Lanzarote, Spain

Air and sea both hover around 68ºF/20ºC in winter, ideal for Papagayo and Playa Blanca beaches or the volcanic pools at Arrieta and Punta Mujeres. Surf at Famara, see Cesar Manrique’s Jameos del Agua, Casa LagOmar and Mirador del Río, hike Timanfaya National Park and explore the 20,000-year-old Cueva de los Verdes. Suggested by: Inês from Randomtrip.net

22. Tenerife, Spain

December days run from +18°C to +25°C, with the south warmer than the north and evenings near +16°C, so bring a jumper too. Without the summer heat it is a great time for excursions, above all to Teide National Park and the active volcano Teide, more than 3,500 meters high. Suggested by: Alexandra from Tenerife-is

23. Nice, France

Nice is cheaper and quieter in December than in summer. Take in the coast from Castle Hill, browse the month-long Christmas market with about 60 stalls, or make a short trip to Monaco. Suggested by: Kristin of Global Travel Escapades

24. Sicily, Italy

Expect mild days of 55-60°F, some rain and rarely snow. Christmas markets run in Palermo, Catania, Ragusa and Agrigento, and low-season prices make it a good time to see Palermo and the Late Baroque Towns of Val di Noto. Suggested by: Soumya of Stories by Soumya

25. Malaga, Spain

With December highs of 17.5 degrees Celsius and little rain, Malaga suits sightseeing and hiking. Visit the Alcazaba and Roman Theatre, the cathedral, Gibralfaro Castle and the Picasso Museum, then catch the nightly Christmas Light Show and the nativity scenes. Suggested By: Cristina of My Little World of Travelling

🌳 Best Christmas Free Breaks in Europe

These getaways suit anyone who wants a December break somewhere Christmas is celebrated far less.

26. Cappadocia, Türkiye

Winter thins the summer crowds in Cappadocia’s lunar valleys, and lower rates make it the time to try a cave hotel in Goreme or Uchisar, often with an open fire. The Goreme Open Air Museum, horse riding and hot air balloon flights all carry on through December. Suggested by: Heather from Conversant Traveller

27. Antalya, Türkiye

Antalya is one of Europe’s warmest spots in December and works well for the school holidays. We had mixed weather but loved our all-inclusive hotel with a heated pool and a day at the Land of Legends Theme Park, and the Christmas touches there were fairly low-key.

28. Ephesus, Türkiye

On the sunny Aegean coast, ancient Ephesus sees about 10 to 14 C (50 to 57 F) in December, little chance of snow and far fewer crowds. Highlights include the Temple of Artemis, the Library of Celsus, the Ancient Theater and the Terrace Houses, ideally with a guide. Suggested by: Kedi from Let’s Travel to Türkiye

I hope this has helped you with the best places to visit in Europe in December
